# Lab overview

R automatically changes (coerces) data types when you combine values that do not all have the same type. Understanding this behavior prevents silent errors in analysis and visualization.

```{r photo, fig.margin = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 5, fig.cap = "Data Coercion Figure — Hands-on Programming in R, G. Grolemund", eval = TRUE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/data-coercion.png")
```

## Learning goals

By the end of this lab, you should be able to:

A. Predict the data type of a vector that mixes values of different types.
B. Use `typeof()` to check the type of an object.
C. Explain why R coerces values when they are combined.
D. Identify variables in a real data frame that can be coerced without loss of information.
E. Recognize visualization problems that arise from incorrect data types.

# Exercises

For each exercise: complete the matching section in `lab-04-starter.Rmd`, run the code, and write any requested interpretation in complete sentences.

## Exercise 1 — Mixed numeric and character

**Goal:** Observe coercion when a character value is combined with numbers.

The same three chunks are present in Exercise 1 in your starter file. Under the first chunk, state the data type of each individual value. Under the second chunk, explain why the combined vector has a different type. Uncomment the `typeof()` line and state the type of the combined vector.

```{r ex1-values, echo = FALSE}
1
1L
"C"
```

```{r ex1-combined, echo = FALSE}
c(1, 1L, "C")
```

```{r ex1-typeof, echo = FALSE}
#typeof(c(1, 1L, "C"))
```

### Exercise 1 checkpoint

🧶 ✅ ⬆️ **Knit, commit, and push.** Suggested commit message: `Complete Exercise 1`.

**Goal:** Anticipate plotting issues caused by an incorrect type.

If we coerced `year` to type *character*, what visualization problems may arise if we tried to recreate the Homework 1 plot that mapped `year` to the x-axis and `richter` to the y-axis?

## Exercise 10 — Create and filter a major-earthquake indicator

**Goal:** Build a logical indicator, coerce it to numeric, and filter.

Copy the chunk into Exercise 10, label it, and complete it so that it:

- creates a new variable called `major` that is `TRUE` when `richter > 7.5`
- coerces the new variable to numeric
- filters to keep only the major earthquakes

```{r label-me, eval = FALSE}
___ %>% 
  mutate(major = case_when(
    ___ > 7.5 ~ TRUE,
    TRUE ~ ___
  )) %>% 
  mutate(___ = as.numeric(___)) %>% 
  filter(___ == ___)
```

Remember to set `eval = TRUE` in the starter file so the chunk runs when you Knit.

**Question:** How many major earthquakes are there in this dataset? Add your response as text.
